provenance.method: nidirect Your rights in health and Your local doctor (GP), plus HSC Northern Ireland Making Communication Accessible for All guidance, checked on 2026-09-01. The resource uses Northern Ireland disability-discrimination framing and records access routes without deciding an individual legal or clinical case.

name: Northern Ireland — healthcare communication access guidance
description: Northern Ireland public guidance on disabled people's access to health services, usable information formats and longer GP appointments for communication needs, alongside HSC staff guidance on communication-accessible services.
intended_use: Prepare for asking a Northern Ireland health service about accessible information, communication support or extra appointment time and understand the national disability-access context.
audience_or_context: Disabled people and people with communication support needs using health and social care services in Northern Ireland, plus staff supporting accessible communication.
limitations: Northern Ireland disability-access law and guidance differ from Great Britain; Equality Act 2010 wording should not be imported into this route.
The HSC communication guide is staff-facing and supports service practice rather than establishing a personalised entitlement.
The form and availability of an adjustment can depend on what is reasonable and on the service context.
This listing is not personalised legal or clinical advice.
cost_or_access_notes: nidirect and HSC Northern Ireland guidance are publicly available online. People who need more time at a GP appointment are advised by nidirect that they should be able to book a longer appointment.
conflicts_of_interest: nidirect and HSC Northern Ireland are first-party public-sector sources for this route; ND Oracle records access information without deciding an individual provider dispute.
